rule: Chapter 4 runtime decisions, D-C4-1..D-C4-13 (the chapter-scoped prefix follows chapters 2 and 3). D-C4-1..7 record C4-M1's dispositions; D-C4-8..12 record C4-M2's; D-C4-13 records the test-independence milestone (TI-1). Each carries its basis in the chapter-0/1 registers and the executing proof in the suite.

decisions.question: How the obj-16 CandidateReceipt is admitted and what anchors candidate immutability.
decisions.disposition: The git_adapter mints from the Sequencer's candidate_state read surface plus cap-42's tree capture; freeze_candidate validates canonical-form bytes, the mirrored schema, and EQUALITY of every ledger-derivable member (attempt identity at the current fence, attempt_contract_hash, all three record tiers, finalization_class, the AttemptContract's frozen source_state, the admitted artifact triples) inside the one t-a05/t-s07 transaction, then commits the attempt_candidates row — ONE per attempt by unique index. The row plus the content-addressed bytes are the immutability anchor: later workspace or repository drift cannot reach the verification subject.

decisions.question: The candidate-tree rule per finalization class, and where the tree-ish comes from.
decisions.disposition: SOURCE_MODIFYING work binds the candidate Git tree identity (rev-parse <tree-ish>^{tree}, 40- or 64-hex object names); READ_ONLY work gains NO invented tree (D-37 absence) and refuses a repository at capture. In the Taskforce flow the SM tree-ish is the specialist's PROPOSED new value from the effect proposal; an SM attempt with no capturable tree stays FINISHED as a visible wait, never a fabricated candidate.

decisions.question: The registered verifier result protocol and the outcome vocabulary mapping.
decisions.disposition: A registered verifier reports by exiting 0 and printing, as its LAST stdout line, {"autobot_verifier_result": {"conclusion": "PASS"|"FAIL"}}. Translation: exit 0 + PASS -> obj-19 PASS; exit 0 + FAIL -> obj-20 FAIL (verifier_reported_fail; the only arm that drives repair); exit != 0 -> obj-20 INCONCLUSIVE (verifier_execution_failed); exit 0 without a typed conclusion -> obj-20 INCONCLUSIVE (malformed_verifier_result). INCONCLUSIVE satisfies nothing and routes to t-s12 unknown. No protocol outcomes were invented for exit codes, and prose ('tests passed') is never a conclusion (INV-06).

decisions.question: What the obj-19/obj-20 admission validates.
decisions.disposition: Canonical-form bytes, the kind's mirrored schema, kind<->outcome agreement, the verifier_runner minter, and EQUALITY of every binding against durable ledger facts: attempt identity at the CURRENT fence (a stale or foreign receipt has no authority, INV-18), attempt_contract_hash, record_hash, the attempt's one admitted obj-16 address, the attempt's one admitted obj-18 address, the D-47 assertion part reference and declared verifier, and the frozen record's bound registration (object hash, registration_id, artifact_root). This seam is INV-17's enforcement point (CH4-verification-binding); refusals commit nothing.

decisions.question: F-C4-1 (this chapter's adversarial finding): can a fully bound receipt claim an outcome its evidence does not support?
decisions.disposition: No longer: the admission resolves the execution output bytes (execution.output_sha256) from the content store and requires the claimed outcome to agree with them under the result protocol; recovery re-verifies the same consistency on every verifier-produced row. RESIDUAL, recorded: in the interim in-process topology (D-01) a writer with content-store access could plant consistent evidence; the target authority-service identity (Chapter 8) closes the caller boundary. The registered INV-06 proof stands on the full stack: SEM-16 eligibility, the typed protocol, the minter gates, the binding admission and this evidence consistency.

decisions.question: The closure dispatch discipline and the t-s12 arm mapping.
decisions.disposition: Before any execution the runner recomputes artifact_root (SEM-15), proves every leaf's exact bytes exist in the content store (D-66 re-hash), and proves the live interpreter identity equals the registration's interpreter_id. Any divergence is an IntegrityHalt that commits nothing — never a substitution (no PATH lookup, no same-named file, no other version); the durable halt is t-s12 bound_artifact_unavailable. Packaged closures are unexecutable in v1 and HALT. Environment mismatch is t-s12 env_mismatch and executes nothing; INCONCLUSIVE conclusions are t-s12 unknown; the repair-budget exhaustion arm stays t-s12 budget_exhausted. Admitted registrations' closure leaves are referenced content in recovery (INV-58's storage half).

decisions.question: The attestation boundary in the chapter-4 receipt plane.
decisions.disposition: Unchanged from D-52/D-53: HUMAN_ATTESTED assertions pass only through your ManualAttestation.ASSERTION, which the verifier runner never mints or touches; no obj-19 is produced for an attested assertion in v1 — the admitted rows are t-s10's consumption surface, and obj-19's result_source is the constant BY_VERIFIER. The BY_ATTESTATION receipt arm is deferred to the chapter that consumes it at acceptance (Chapter 5), recorded here so the schema bump is an append, not a correction. [C4-M2 executed exactly the recorded append: see D-C4-11.]

decisions.question: The role-transform check's result model and the admission's re-derivation discipline (INV-44/INV-49, C4-M2).
decisions.disposition: The check is a BY_VERIFIER result over a D-47 ROLE_TRANSFORM part {record, ROLE_TRANSFORM, role}; its ledger row key is 'role-transform/<role>' (the name_id grammar forbids '/', so no assertion id can collide) under the existing one-row-per-key unique index. The receipt carries the bound TransformRegistration in the registration block and a transform_check block {input_name, input_sha256, expected_sha256 when the transform completed, observed_sha256 when admitted producer evidence carries the child's received prompt identity}. Its basis vocabulary is its own: FAIL exists only as transform_output_mismatch (completed transform, present UNEQUAL identities — the repair path); INCONCLUSIVE is verifier_execution_failed (nonzero exit; no expected output exists) or missing_producer_evidence (completed transform, NO admitted obj-11 carries a prompt identity). Admission is D-C3-2 grade: for every completed-transform claim the seam RE-EXECUTES the bound closure over the frozen record's single declared specification input (the v1 binding is defined over exactly ONE) and refuses an expected identity it did not just re-derive; the OBSERVED identity is derived only from admitted obj-11 producer bytes (exactly one distinct recorded identity; several distinct are an ambiguity refusal; a claim matching nothing admitted is refused). A claimed execution FAILURE is not re-executed (a failure cannot be forced to reproduce); it binds, couples (expected absent, nonzero exit) and concludes nothing. conclude_verification requires the admitted check (PASS unlocks; FAIL drives t-a08/t-s11 like any row; INCONCLUSIVE blocks to t-s12 unknown) whenever the frozen record declares a transform for the DISPATCHED role.

decisions.question: Retention at recovery: report or halt when a live record's bound closure leaves are missing?
decisions.disposition: REPORT, never a recovery halt: recover() returns retention.missing_bound_leaves = [{sequence_id, registration, leaf}] for every NON-terminal sequence whose bound registrations' closure leaves do not resolve. The fail-closed act stays dispatch-time INV-53 (resolve_closure HALTs over a missing leaf and never substitutes). Rationale: the chapter-1 fixture registrations are identity vectors with no executable bytes — a runtime holding such records (the admission corpus) must stay recoverable, with every gap visible the moment restart runs; recovery HALTs on impossible COMBINATIONS of committed facts, not on missing future-use bytes.

decisions.question: Which packaged closure form executes, and what the image form does (C4-M2).
decisions.disposition: The SUPPORTED form is {kind: packaged, manifest_sha256} where the manifest bytes are a PackageManifest v1 {schema_version: v1, kind: PackageManifest, entries: [{path, content_sha256}], entrypoint (one of the entries), interpreter_id optional}: every entry materializes from the content store at its RELATIVE slash path (grammar fails closed: no absolute paths, no '..', no backslashes, no duplicates), only the bound entrypoint executes (registration and manifest entrypoints must AGREE), and a pinned interpreter_id must equal the live identity (INV-66). The {kind: packaged, image_digest} form names a container image; no container engine is part of this runtime's frozen environment, so it HALTs explicitly (bound_artifact_unavailable) rather than being approximated by another closure kind — the directive's 'do not pretend to support an execution mechanism the runtime cannot actually execute', honored in the refusing direction. One resolver and one materializer (autobot.transforms) serve verifier executions and transform executions alike; native/python/packaged share the discipline, with execution parity proven for python and packaged (no native binary exists in the corpus to execute; native parity is proven at resolution/materialization). [TI-1 tightened the entry-path grammar after F-TI-6 — the wording above did not hold on Windows: see D-C4-13.]

decisions.question: The BY_ATTESTATION arm and the obj-37 admission reshape (C4-M2).
decisions.disposition: attest_assertion is now the obj-37 ADMISSION seam: it validates the upgraded D-53 bindings (identity: attested_by you; provenance: attests PASS; FULL scope: attempt_id + attempt_contract_hash + the admitted obj-16 candidate_receipt_sha256 + the D-47 part reference {record, ASSERTION, assertion_id}), stores the exact bytes (D-31; the D-29 kind-grammar finding still applies, so the dotted kind is preserved by bytes, never object-hashed) and writes the attempt_attestations row (schema v10, one per (attempt, assertion)) with journal ch4:admit-attestation — it no longer writes a verification row. The verifier runner INCORPORATES an admitted attestation into the canonical obj-19 BY_ATTESTATION arm {attestation_sha256, outcome ATTESTED, mode HUMAN_ATTESTED, NO registration/execution/environment — an attestation is a human act and is never dressed up as an execution} and submits it through register_attested_result, which re-validates every binding including byte-address equality with the ADMITTED attestation; the row's authority principal is you, never the incorporating runner. Attestation remains durable BEFORE conclude can commit t-s10. Chapter-5 boundary untouched: acceptance still consumes PASS/ATTESTED rows; no acceptance semantics were added. Note: an environment_constraint declared on a HUMAN_ATTESTED assertion constrains nothing (no execution exists to constrain) — a documented vocabulary boundary, not an authority grant.

decisions.question: F-C4-2: the environment-variable constraint vocabulary spelling.
decisions.disposition: The FROZEN task_contract_record and obj-10 schemas spell the env-var constraint section 'env'; C4-M1's environment_satisfies matched a section spelled 'env_vars', which the frozen records cannot even represent — a frozen 'env' constraint hit the unsupported-section fail-closed branch (no false accept; the registered vocabulary was unimplementable). Fixed in C4-M2: the constraint section is 'env' (matched against the obj-18 CAPTURE field 'env_vars', whose spelling is the frozen chapter-1 capture schema's); a constraint section spelled 'env_vars' now fails closed explicitly as unsupported. The D-56 vocabulary proof covers both directions.

decisions.question: TI-1: what makes a runtime-suite proof independent, what an oracle's disagreement becomes, and what the independence harness is allowed to change.
decisions.disposition: The chapter-1 D-58 standard applies to the runtime suite. An expected value or a state read counts as INDEPENDENT only when it is produced by code that imports nothing from autobot or contract_library — enforced per oracle by an import allowlist scan, a dynamic-import token ban and a fresh -I interpreter import graph. The harness is tests/autobot preimage2 (identity constructions, written from the frozen chapter-1 documents and proven against the frozen goldens before it is compared with the library), auditor2 (one runtime directory's journal chain, D-68 pairing, content references, identities, receipt bindings and retention reachability, over its own read-only connection, in process and in a fresh process; an unreadable directory is never a clean one and every clean report carries a journal witness), transform2 (the calibrated A1 rule twice more, by unlike mechanisms) and real_bytes (the local-only reader of the operator's retained provider records). An oracle that disagrees with production is NEVER aligned to it: the disagreement is a numbered finding with one of two dispositions. Either the defect is fixed at the narrowest seam and the failing oracle is named — F-TI-1 (Registry.admit_object refuses a TaskContractRecord: its object hash is the record_hash tier, D-29/D-33, never the flat hash), F-TI-4 (reclaim refuses the journaled finalization receipts and the receipt-bound execution evidence recovery resolves), F-TI-6 (the closure-path grammar) — or it is recorded and pinned by a test that fails the moment the behavior changes, because the correction belongs to a frozen chapter or to the operator: F-TI-2 (the library restricts tier preimages at top level only; unreachable under the closed schema), F-TI-3 (the object-kind grammar is enforced but documented nowhere) and F-TI-5 below. The harness changes no authority semantics and no schema. The mutation matrix (tests/autobot/mutation_matrix.json, enforced by test_mutation_matrix.py) is the registry of refusals: every refusal assertion in the suite is a row tying invariant, seam, planted defect, named refusal, test and control; every target invariant has a row whose marker is pinned by an assertion (never by prose); a new refusal assertion without a row fails the suite. These are planted-defect proofs; classical code-mutation testing is out of scope. Real provider or governance bytes are never committed without the operator's approval per file: the default is the local-only arm (AUTOBOT_REAL_BYTES=require makes absence a failure on the host that holds the evidence) plus a committed manifest of sha256 identities only. The closure-path grammar, superseding the entry-path wording of D-C4-10: a closure path is a frozen D-26 RepoPath that names the same plain file on every filesystem — no segment carrying a less-than, greater-than, colon, double-quote, pipe, question-mark or asterisk character (so no drive letter and no stream suffix), a trailing dot, a Windows device name or the 8.3 short-alias form; no first segment the runner itself writes into the run directory (input.bin, output.bin, context.json, subject); no two entries equal under case folding; none both a file and a directory of another. It is applied to manifest entries at resolution (IntegrityHalt, t-s12 bound_artifact_unavailable) and to every entrypoint at materialization, before anything is written; the frozen D-26 grammar itself is unchanged. OPEN, for the operator — F-TI-5: the obj-12 recognizer extracts NO fact from the governance producer's real records (UTF-8 with a byte order mark; the decision spelled verdict), so the INV-68 integrity classes cannot see real producer bytes, and reading past the mark alone would classify every governed execution an orphan; framing, spelling and the verdict vocabulary must be ruled on together under D-C3-5, D-C3-6 and D-C3-8. Recorded and pinned (test_real_boundary.GovernanceRecognizerDivergenceTests), deliberately not corrected here.
